Like many science fiction films that preceded actual manned space flight, this movie gets a lot of technical things wrong. However, it gets a lot of things right that other films failed to anticipate. For example, can you think of other films that depicted trained career astronauts as being anything other than white males? In this film, Al, an experienced black astronaut who acts as a mentor to the visiting journalist, is described by the station commander as "the best there is." Al not only comes up with the solution for stopping the menacing spacecraft that threatens to end life on Earth…

Like many Japanese films dubbed by Americans with no knowledge of science, it comes off as worse than it originally was. Flowers that change hydrogen to oxygen? Obviously meant to be carbon dioxide to oxygen, but they were more concerned with matching dialogue with the lip-movements of the actors than getting things right. This explains many of the strange turns-of-phrase you find in these foreign films. By the way, "Galaxy M-12" was the name of the space station, which was never mentioned again in the rest of the film. 2 stars for bad dubbing, 5 stars for period SFX, -1 star for a meteoroid…

TheExecutioner1955: An episode of popular 1950s anthology series "Four Star Playhouse" titled "The Executioner". Starring Charles Boyer. Originally broadcast 9 June 1955.
FourStarPlayhouse-EddiesPlace: An episode of anthology series "Four Star Playhouse". This episode was originally broadcast 10 March 1955 on CBS. This however is a syndication print under the "Star Performance" title. Episode stars Ida Lupino, William Talman, and Kathryn Card. This episode was also repeated under the titles "Golden Playhouse" and "Presenting Ida Lupino".

rv: Ida Lupino is terrific in this one, as always. Good turns from secondary actors, especially William " Hamilton Berger" Talman and Katharine Card. Talman was also in the Hitchhiker, which Lupino directed. Very indicative of the times, when a man could slap around a woman and get away with it.

FourStarPlayhouse-DarkMeeting: An episode of "Four Star Playhouse" titled "Dark Meeting". Originally broadcast on CBS on 5 January 1956, this however is a syndication print under the "Star Performance" title, but still runs approx 25 minutes. Episode stars Ida Lupino, Warren Stevens and Elliott Reid.

rv: Lonely bowling alley owner Billie (Lupino) hires creepy, possessive Warren Stevens after he shows up for a job she's listed in the paper, not bothering with an interview or asking for references. Childhood pal and cafe manager Barney (Reid) is a little more wary, especially when his mom points out a familiar face on the cover of the newspaper. Might have worked better as an hour thriller, with more background on the new hire.

WithNoOneToH: Documantary demonstrating how the formation of a food-buying club by a group of Newark welfare mothers brought about a necessary change in the community. Nice images of African-American neighborhood in Newark.

rv: A low-key, straightforward piece about the attempts of neighborhood women on welfare to organize a buying club, due to overpricing of items to welfare recipients. This film is basically a long video showing some of the group's meetings and discussions. Few cuts; no real 'theatrical' quality, doesn't appear to have been scripted. Narration is by one of the women on the committee. Doesn't really discuss the issues underlying. Seems vaguely sanitized, but when the black women enter a warehouse staffed by largely white men you can feel a subtle hint of tension. Hints of resistance and…
